# Public recovery fixtures

Every seed, password, key and address in this directory is public synthetic test
data. Never send funds to these addresses or use these seeds in a real wallet.
The tests never open or discover a user's wallet.

`native_sdk_keys.json` was generated by `generate_native_keys.rs` using the
Stashi native SDK, independently of this Python recovery implementation. It
contains accounts 0 and 7 of one public BIP39 vector and account 0 of a different
public vector, used as a separately imported spending key. The expected Sapling
key encodings and addresses come from the SDK, not the recovery parser.

The SDK checkout used was
`0a1faba95cee76f1cbda52337d5b136ba85374ae`. Its Sapling key implementation is
unchanged from the published
[`v1.2.6` source](https://github.com/PirateNetwork/Pirate-Unified-Light-Wallet/tree/dedf63381996c5770945d16a4afa63ec7e35a676/crates/pirate-core/src/keys.rs).

To regenerate the fixture, build the SDK's `pirate-core`, `pirate-params` and
`zcash_client_backend` libraries using its locked Cargo workspace in `crates/`.
Compile `generate_native_keys.rs` with Rust 2021, pass that build's dependency
directory using `-L dependency=...`, and pass the three matching library files
with `--extern pirate_core=...`, `--extern pirate_params=...` and
`--extern zcash_client_backend=...`. Run the generator with an explicit new
output filename; it refuses to overwrite an existing file. This developer-only
generator is not bundled or run by the recovery application.

The Python tests build native key-section prefixes in memory following the
pinned Lite writer. These prefixes are not complete transaction databases.
They exercise seed encryption, imported-key encryption, viewing-only and HD
records, old format versions, corrupt records and unrelated damaged cache data.

The [Skull Island fixture notes](skull_island/README.md) give the independently
generated Node AES/HMAC vectors and the upstream format references.
